sources.entry: WriteFreely - Writing software for starting a minimalist, federated blog — or an entire community. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go

summary.one_liner: WriteFreely is a minimalist, federated publishing platform for running a blog or a writing community, deployed as a single Go binary.
summary.what_it_does: WriteFreely provides a plain, auto-saving editor for writing and publishing posts with a distraction-free layout. It supports multiple blogs per account, draft posts, and publishing to several blogs from one account. Posts can be categorized with hashtags, and normal posts can be pinned to create static pages. It federates with other ActivityPub-powered software, including WriteFreely and Plume, and supports OAuth 2.0 for bringing in members from existing platforms. The README says blog elements are localized in 20+ languages, with support for non-Latin and right-to-left scripts. It runs on built-in SQLite or on MySQL/MariaDB.
use_cases: Run a private or public writing community
Publish under multiple pen names from one account
Host a federated blog that interacts with ActivityPub software
how_to_run: Download a pre-built binary for your platform (see the installation guide)
Choose SQLite (built in) or add a MySQL or MariaDB database
Follow the installation guide on writefreely.org to configure and start the server
For Docker, see the Docker guide referenced in the README
For development, follow the developer setup guide
notable: Federated via ActivityPub, interoperating with WriteFreely, Plume, and other ActivityPub software
Ships as a static binary on any platform and architecture Go supports
Multiple blogs per account for different pen names without public linkage
Pin posts to turn them into static pages
First-class support for non-Latin and right-to-left scripts
caveats: The README points to Write.as, a hosted service from the same team, as the quickest deployment route; it is a paid-or-managed alternative to self-hosting
Self-hosting requires setting up the binary or a database yourself; the README refers to external guides for installation and Docker
